concept: FileUpload is a key that opens the system picker, and under it each chosen file read out in its own small window: the name on the left, the size on the right, and a remove key beside the window. It reports the files and does nothing else; sending them is the product's job.

default_to_avoid.pattern: file upload dropzone: a dashed-border box with a cloud icon and the words drag and drop files here, orange browse link inside
default_to_avoid.why_not: A dashed box is a bordered rectangle floating on the page and spends the unit's orange on a link; the key already says what to press, and the files are readings, so they sit in windows.

default_to_avoid.pattern: file upload list as rows with a coloured file-type tile and a red trash icon
default_to_avoid.why_not: Tiles and trash icons add a second visual language; the name and size are the information, and remove is one plain key with a name.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): each reading stands in its own window cut into the body, and the keys sit outside the windows
system/FORM.md display class: window recessed into the body, value right-aligned and the unit beside it
packages/react/src/components/Button, IconButton, HelperText, Progress: the key, the remove key, the message lines and the optional per-file groove are those parts imported as they are

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: Each chosen file stands in a window that takes surface.sunken and elevation.well, so a file reads as a reading and never as a key.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The choose key, each window and each remove key are at least control.md tall, so a row is one 44px strip and the remove key is never smaller.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: The choose key and each remove key are real buttons reached by Tab and pressed with Space or Enter; after a removal focus moves to the next remove key, or back to the choose key.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The choose key is a plain key and the windows are ink, so FileUpload spends no orange and leaves it to the unit's own primary key.

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: The message lines and the removal note sit in polite live regions, and a window itself takes no focus and does nothing when pressed.

options.name: one well holds the key and the rows

variants.reason: C makes each file a reading in its own window, with the remove key outside on the body, as FORM.md puts keys outside displays; A sets a raised key inside a recess and looks like an Input, and B has no form of its own and drifts to the generic attachment list.

root.why: The label, key, hint, windows and messages stack in one column on the body's inset line, with gaps and no rules between them.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight above the key, and it names the group for assistive tech.

list.why: A list of rows kept apart by gaps, so the count of files is read out and the layout does not reflow between files.

item.why: One file is a window and its remove key in a two-column strip, 44px tall at least, so both ends of the row are full-size targets.

window.why: The recess takes the inverse light and holds the name, the size and the optional groove, so the file reads as a reading.

name.why: The file name is body size in primary ink with a line box tall enough for Thai marks, and a long name wraps instead of being cut.

size.why: The size is printed right-aligned in the caption size with tabular figures, in secondary ink at more than 4.5:1.

progress.why: The optional Progress groove spans the window under the name and size, so the sending state is told inside the same reading.

issues.why: The error lines stand under the list in a polite live region, so a refused file is announced without moving focus.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled FileUpload loses the recess shadow of its windows and fades to half, and its keys are disabled, so it reads as not taking files now.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours each window keeps a real border in the text colour, so the files stay separate without a shadow.
